Outcasts
out´kăsts
n. pl. (those driven out; the banished of Israel; Hebrew nadach)
From out and cast — those thrown out. The Hebrew participle niddach means driven away or banished, and in the prophets it is almost a technical term for the scattered of the covenant people.

Biblical Definition

Outcasts in Scripture are the driven-away of God's people, and He never speaks of them as lost. The psalmist joins the word to the building of the city: “The LORD doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Israel” (Psa 147:2). Isaiah makes their gathering the work of the messianic ensign: “And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth” (Isa 11:12), and again at the trumpet: “they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt, and shall worship the LORD in the holy mount at Jerusalem” (Isa 27:13). He also commands a nation to shelter them: “Take counsel, execute judgment… hide the outcasts; bewray not him that wandereth” (Isa 16:3), and “Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler” (Isa 16:4). Note the possessive: mine outcasts. And Jeremiah records what the nations called Zion and what the LORD answered: “because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after” (Jer 30:17) — and the same verse begins, I will restore health unto thee.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines an outcast as one who is cast out or expelled; an exile; one driven from home or country; and, in Scripture, a person rejected of men.

expand to see more

OUTCAST, pp. Cast out; thrown away; rejected as useless.

OUTCAST, n. One who is cast out or expelled; an exile; one driven from home or country.

2. In Scripture, one banished or driven away, but not forgotten of God.

Key Scripture

Psa 147:2 — "The LORD doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Israel."

Isa 11:12 — "And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth."

Isa 16:4 — "Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler: for the extortioner is at an end, the spoiler ceaseth, the oppressors are consumed out of the land."

Jer 30:17 — "For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the LORD; because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after."

Modern Corruption

The marginalized are made an autonomous political category, while Scripture calls the driven-away God's own and holds their scattering to be His judgment and their gathering His work.

expand to see more

Scripture has a great deal to say about the driven-away, and none of it fits the modern category of the marginalized as an identity that confers moral standing. Isaiah's outcasts are outcasts because God scattered them for covenant-breaking; they remain mine outcasts while scattered; and their gathering is accomplished by an ensign lifted up for the nations, not by their own assertion. The biblical categories are the exile, the stranger, the widow, the fatherless and the afflicted, and each of them is defined by what God says and does, not by a position in a social hierarchy.

What Scripture does demand is concrete and costly. Isaiah 16 orders Moab — a hostile nation — to hide the outcasts, to be a covert to them from the face of the spoiler, and not to betray the one who wanders. That is a command to shelter refugees of a people not one's own, issued to a nation under judgment, and the chapter goes on to pronounce Moab's doom partly for pride. The church that will not shelter the driven-away has failed a test that was once set for Moab.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew nadach (H5080), to drive away, banish; the passive participle niddach is the prophets' word for the outcasts; qabats (H6908), to gather, is always the answer to it.

expand to see more

Hebrew nadach (H5080) — to drive out, banish; Isaiah 11:12, 16:3, 27:13.

Hebrew qabats (H6908) — to gather; Psalm 147:2, he gathereth together the outcasts.

Hebrew nes (H5251) — ensign, banner; lifted for the nations, Isaiah 11:12.

Hebrew sether (H5643) — covert, hiding place; be thou a covert to them, Isaiah 16:4.

Hebrew 'arukah (H724) — healing, restoration; I will restore health unto thee, Jeremiah 30:17.

Usage

"“He gathereth together the outcasts of Israel” — in the same verse as building the city."

"“Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab” — and the possessive is the point."

"“They called thee an Outcast… I will restore health unto thee” — the world's name, God's answer."
